| mass-properties.fraction-bit-count-bound | law: Default | structural | — | The type's own remarks: 'Every count must lie in [0, MaximumFractionBitCount]; a count outside it is refused rather than rounded.' This pins the boundary the remarks state, at both members the bound gates. TryInvertMass at fractionBitsMass == MaximumFractionBitCount (mass = 2^(bound-2), fractionBitsOut = 0) must be ADMITTED to the arithmetic — the reciprocal 2^bound/2^(bound-2) is the exact integer 4 with nothing to round, so a bare 'true, 4' return is proof the guard let the count through rather than merely a resolution refusal that a bound refusal would look identical to from outside. TrySphereBody at all four scales == MaximumFractionBitCount, with density = 0, is likewise admitted: every numerator folds to zero regardless of radius or scale, so 'true, (0,0)' is guaranteed once the guard is passed and proves nothing else. Moving either member's fraction bit count to MaximumFractionBitCount + 1, or to -1, with every other operand held at the admitted case's values, must refuse outright — both TryInvertMass's out parameter and TrySphereBody's mass and inertia are checked to be exactly zero on every refusal, never the last successful value left behind | — | — | — |
| mass-properties.inversion-refuses-below-resolution | law: Default | structural | — | The inversions decline rather than answer a zero a caller would read as a physical claim. TryInvertMass at mass = long.MaxValue with both scales at zero must refuse, because the correctly rounded reciprocal is zero and answering it would silently declare the body immovable; a zero mass must refuse outright; and a unit mass at Q16 must invert to EXACTLY 65536 at Q16, so the law pins the boundary rather than merely observing a refusal. TryInvertInertia at a diagonal 2^40 tensor with both scales at zero must refuse for the same reason — every entry of the true inverse is below one half — while the Q16 identity tensor must invert to the Q16 identity tensor exactly. Every refusal is checked to leave all six outputs at zero | — | — | — |
| mass-properties.parallel-axis-vs-oracle | law: Default | shared-substrate | transcription | FixedMassProperties.TryTranslateInertia — the parallel-axis transfer I' = I + m(\|d\|^2*delta - d(x)d) of a symmetric tensor to a parallel frame, all six distinct entries, each rounded once | Oracles.TryTranslateInertia, which states the general tensor form with \|d\|^2 formed ONCE as dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 and each diagonal entry taken as that total minus its own squared component, where the subject writes each diagonal entry's own pre-expanded pair (dy^2 + dz^2, and so on). A mis-assigned axis in that expansion is what the difference catches | the parallel-axis theorem itself: the reference TRANSCRIBES the same identity rather than deriving the transferred tensor independently, so a wrong theorem — as opposed to a wrong expansion, a wrong scale or a wrong sign on the outer product — would be invisible to this comparison | The independent witness is mass-properties.capsule-vs-oracle, whose oracle applies this same theorem TWICE from first principles (flat face to hemisphere centroid, centroid to capsule centre) and reaches a coefficient the subject states independently; agreement there is evidence the theorem as applied is right, not merely transcribed consistently |
| mass-properties.parallel-axis-vs-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | The transfer's stored entry is lifted onto the mass term's own denominator by a LOSSLESS shift before the addition, so only the narrowing rounds; the law's fold keeps masses strictly positive and offsets inside a sixteen-bit signed band, and physical realizability of the input tensor is deliberately NOT imposed — the kernel does not require it and the law does not pretend it does. A refusal leaves every one of the six outputs at zero | — | — | — |
| mass-properties.pinned-pi-is-correctly-rounded | law: Default | classical | — | FixedQ4816.PiQ61 — the ONE constant the mass-property subject and its oracles share, and therefore the one value the family's agreement laws cannot themselves check | Oracles.Pi's Machin enclosure at 128 bits, derived by this suite from an alternating arctangent series rather than transcribed from any digit table. The enclosure's two ends are each reduced to 61 fraction bits; the law REQUIRES them to agree before deciding, so the verdict is a decision rather than an estimate, and then requires the pinned raw to equal that common value | — | — |
| mass-properties.pinned-pi-is-correctly-rounded | law: Default | structural | — | This is what makes the shared constant a pinned value rather than an assumption. The substitution itself remains an envelope the mass-property kernels carry openly: every result is the exact rational value of its formula WITH this rational in place of pi, rounded once — a relative departure below 2^-62, and the only inexactness in FixedMassProperties | — | — | — |
| mass-properties.sphere-vs-oracle | law: Default | classical | — | FixedMassProperties.TrySphereBody — the mass and the isotropic inertia of a solid sphere about its centre, each one rounding of its own exact rational at independently swept density, length, mass and inertia scales | Oracles.TrySphereBody, which takes the inertia as (2/5)*M*r^2 against the EXACT rational mass, where the subject collapses the whole chain into (8/15)*rho*pi*r^5. The two routes reach the same rational by different constant folds, so a mis-folded 8/15 cannot appear in both | — | — |
| mass-properties.sphere-vs-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | Same shared-pi declaration and same fold envelope as mass-properties.volumes-vs-oracle. The refusal contract is 'false AND every output at zero', asserted against the subject directly on every declining draw | — | — | — |
| mass-properties.volumes-vs-oracle | law: Default | classical | — | FixedMassProperties.TrySphereVolume, TryBoxVolume, TryCylinderVolume and TryCapsuleVolume (internal) — all four exercised on every draw, each one rounding of the exact rational volume at a swept output scale — together with the shared FixedPointRounding.TryRoundRational kernel each of those roundings divides, tie-breaks and narrows through | Oracles.TryPrimitiveVolume — the same four volumes assembled from the GEOMETRIC definition rather than from the subject's folded constants: the box from its FULL extents (2h in each axis) rather than three half-extents folded into a leading eight, and the capsule as a cylinder PLUS a whole sphere as two separate terms rather than as one collapsed fraction over three. A mis-folded constant in the subject therefore cannot be mirrored in the reference | — | — |
| mass-properties.volumes-vs-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | SHARED CONSTANT, declared: both sides substitute the same pinned rational FixedQ4816.PiQ61 for the transcendental, read from the subject's own declaration rather than transcribed as digits (a transcription would let the two drift while every law stayed green). That the constant IS the correctly rounded pi is decided separately by mass-properties.pinned-pi-is-correctly-rounded against this suite's own Machin enclosure. ENVELOPE: dimensions are folded onto a twenty-bit band and fraction bit counts onto [0, 32] — the accumulation is exact in BigInteger at any width, so a wider fold would buy only carrier refusals; the refusal side of the biconditional is asserted on every draw either way. This family folds its scale into the numerator before dividing, so the shared kernel is reached at a zero fractionBitCount only; its shifting path is driven by Puck.Physics's softness chain, which no law in this suite runs | — | — | — |
| meet.associative | law: Default | structural | — | meet is associative on every shipped attenuation carrier — MeetMask64 (bitwise AND), MeetQuantity64 (minimum) and the product closed at mask times quantity — over full-width edge/random/frontier lane triples reinterpreted as raw bits, so a delegation chain folds to one envelope however it is bracketed; together with meet.commutative this is what makes the chain's fold order-free | — | — | — |
| meet.attenuation-never-widens | law: Default | classical | — | THE SECURITY PROPERTY of the attenuation pipeline, both halves of the greatest-lower-bound statement: Meet(a, b) is at most a and at most b on every shipped carrier, so no attenuation step can widen authority; and any common lower bound of the operands is at most the meet, so attenuation discards nothing both operands allow — the values are constructed from raw lanes and read back through Bits/Amount/First/Second, so a constructor-to-property misroute is observable here too | order spellings independent of the subjects: the mask order is a per-bit shift-walk subset test that never forms the masked-complement expression MeetMask64.IsAtMost is written as, the quantity order is the ulong carrier's primitive numeric comparison, and the greatest-half witnesses are manufactured from raw lane arithmetic rather than by any subject member | — | — |
| meet.bottom-absorbing | law: Default | structural | — | Bottom absorbs the meet on both sides, on every shipped attenuation carrier, over full-width edge/random/frontier lanes: a revoked link — the empty mask, the zero quantity, the pair of both — collapses the whole delegation chain to nothing, whichever side it arrives on; a meet mutated toward union or maximum fails here even though it keeps idempotence, commutativity and associativity | — | — | — |
| meet.commutative | law: Default | structural | — | meet is commutative on every shipped attenuation carrier over full-width edge/random/frontier lane pairs: the two envelopes of a delegation step contribute symmetrically, so which side authored a restriction cannot change what survives the fold — the case a product meet that silently drops one operand's component fails first | — | — | — |
| meet.idempotent | law: Default | structural | — | meet is idempotent on every shipped attenuation carrier over full-width edge/random/frontier lanes: an envelope folded with itself is bit-identically unchanged, so repeating a link in a delegation chain attenuates nothing further — a meet mutated toward any mixing operation (XOR, addition, averaging) fails here | — | — | — |
| meet.order-agrees-with-meet | law: Default | structural | — | the shipped order predicate decides exactly the meet's order on every carrier — a.IsAtMost(b) if and only if Meet(a, b) == a — over the sampled pair plus comparable pairs manufactured through the meet itself, so both truth values are exercised every sweep; both sides of the equivalence are subject members, and the external anchor is meet.attenuation-never-widens, which pins the meet against independently spelled orders, so this coherence transfers that pin onto IsAtMost | — | — | — |
| meet.product-composes-componentwise | law: Default | structural | — | the composition law — a product of meet-semilattices is a meet-semilattice, componentwise: the closed product's Meet, Top, Bottom and IsAtMost each project onto the component carriers' own operations (the order as the conjunction of component orders), and the construction stacks, a product nested inside a product projecting the same way one level up; every projection dispatches through IMeetSemilattice's static abstracts, so this is also where interface dispatch is pinned — component-carrier defects are NOT catchable here (they would appear on both sides) and stand at the other meet.* cases, which sweep the product carrier directly and so transfer the semilattice laws to composed envelopes | — | — | — |
| meet.top-identity | law: Default | structural | — | Top is a two-sided identity for the meet on every shipped attenuation carrier, over full-width edge/random/frontier lanes: an unrestricted link in a delegation chain attenuates nothing, so a chain's fold can start from Top without biasing the result — a meet mutated toward union or maximum fails here even though it keeps idempotence, commutativity and associativity | — | — | — |
| mixed-scale.checked-product-matches-representability | law: Default | classical | — | FusedArithmetic.TryMixedScaleProduct (two factors) — the refuse/succeed verdict AND the returned raw, over the same swept operands as mixed-scale.product-vs-oracle | Oracles.MixedScaleProduct's unwrapped representability verdict: the exact rounded product is compared against the signed 64-bit bounds in arbitrary width, where the subject decides the same question from an overflow flag its own left shift raises plus a magnitude-against-limit test. Agreement pins that the checked face declines EXACTLY where the value leaves the carrier — never earlier (a conservative refusal) and never later (a silent wrap) | — | — |
| mixed-scale.checked-product-matches-representability | law: Default | structural | — | The refusal contract is 'false AND the output at zero', asserted against the SUBJECT directly on every declining draw rather than against the oracle, which could share a defect. Same fold envelope as mixed-scale.product-vs-oracle; shares the mixed-scale domain key with it deliberately, so the wrapping and refusing faces are compared over bit-identical operands | — | — | — |
| mixed-scale.dot-product-vs-oracle | law: Default | classical | — | FusedArithmetic.TryMixedScaleDotProduct — the refuse/succeed verdict and returned raw for the dot product of two three-component raw vectors at independent fixed-point scales, with all three products accumulated before one rounding | Oracles.MixedScaleDotProduct — all three products and their sum formed in BigInteger, then rounded once by RoundRationalTiesToEven against an explicit power-of-two denominator. The subject accumulates sign-plus-UInt128 terms and decides the tie by inspecting discarded bits against a half-unit; no accumulation width or rounding comparison is shared | — | — |
| mixed-scale.dot-product-vs-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | The refusal contract is false with a zero output, asserted directly. ENVELOPE: fraction bit counts are folded onto [0, 64], so this swept law reaches shifts in [-128, 64]; the full three-product magnitude is always below 2^128 because three signed-64 products total at most 3·2^126 | — | — | — |
| mixed-scale.extreme-scale-counts-are-congruent | law: Default | structural | — | PINS THE SHIFT-COUNT CORNERS the swept laws deliberately do not reach, at five hand-derived witnesses. A fraction bit count is an int, so a caller can name a combination whose exponent would wrap in int arithmetic or alias a UInt128 shift count modulo 128. (1) fractionBitsA = fractionBitsB = 64 with fractionBitsOut = 0 shifts right by exactly 128: the largest product two raws form is 2^126, a quarter of the discarded unit, so the correctly rounded result is zero and the checked face must ANSWER it rather than refuse — a masked shift count would instead return the whole magnitude. (2) The same operands at fractionBitsOut = int.MaxValue shift left past the accumulator: the true value is a multiple of 2^64, so the wrapping face is congruent at zero while the checked face refuses. (3) fractionBitsA = int.MinValue drives the exponent to 0 - int.MinValue = 2^31, which stays POSITIVE only because the three counts are combined in long; computed in int it wraps to int.MinValue, turning a left shift into a rounding right shift and answering a different value | — | — | — |
| mixed-scale.product-vs-oracle | law: Default | classical | — | FusedArithmetic.MixedScaleProduct (internal) — the wrapping one-rounding product of two raws carried at DIFFERENT fixed-point scales, over the full signed range of both factors and every fraction bit count in [0, 64] for each of the three scales | Oracles.MixedScaleProduct — the whole product formed in BigInteger at arbitrary width and rounded ONCE against an explicit power-of-two denominator by RoundRationalTiesToEven, which decides the tie by comparing 2r against d. The subject accumulates a sign-plus-UInt128 magnitude and decides the same tie by splitting the discarded bits against a half-unit it forms itself, then wraps the narrowed word; no width, no half-unit and no wrap is shared between the two | — | — |
| mixed-scale.product-vs-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | ENVELOPE: the three fraction bit counts are folded onto [0, 64], so the rounding exponent stays in [-128, 64] and never reaches the shift-count corners (at or past 128 in either direction) where a CLR UInt128 shift would alias modulo 128. Those corners are pinned by mixed-scale.extreme-scale-counts-are-congruent instead, against hand-derived values, because an oracle built from a power-of-two denominator cannot form 2^int.MaxValue | — | — | — |
| mixed-scale.scaled-reciprocal-invalid-inputs-refuse | law: Default | structural | — | FusedArithmetic.TryScaledReciprocal refuses with zero output for zero and negative raws, a negative combined fraction count, a combined count above int.MaxValue, and a count whose exact starting quotient would exceed the UInt128 restoring divider's documented 127-bit margin | — | — | — |
| mixed-scale.scaled-reciprocal-vs-oracle | law: Default | classical | — | FusedArithmetic.TryScaledReciprocal — the refuse/succeed verdict and returned raw for the reciprocal of a positive raw at one fixed-point scale, rounded once onto another | Oracles.ScaledReciprocal — the exact numerator 2^(fractionBitsIn + fractionBitsOut) formed in BigInteger and divided by the positive raw through RoundRationalTiesToEven, which compares 2r against d. The subject uses UInt128 restoring division and compares r against d-r, then narrows separately | — | — |
| mixed-scale.scaled-reciprocal-vs-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | The refusal contract is false with a zero output, asserted directly. ENVELOPE: both swept fraction bit counts are folded onto [0, 62], so their sum stays inside the restoring divider's 127-bit starting-width limit; invalid values and fraction-count extremes answer at mixed-scale.scaled-reciprocal-invalid-inputs-refuse | — | — | — |
| mixed-scale.triple-product-vs-oracle | law: Default | classical | — | FusedArithmetic.TryMixedScaleProduct (THREE factors) — the refuse/succeed verdict and the returned raw for a product of three raws at three independent scales, rounded once | Oracles.MixedScaleTripleProduct — the triple product formed in BigInteger and rounded once, reporting separately whether the exact product's magnitude stays inside 2^128 and whether the rounded value fits the raw. The subject decides the width question by testing the third factor against UInt128.MaxValue divided by the running pair, an exact test rather than a bit-length estimate; the oracle decides it by comparing the exact magnitude against 2^128 directly | — | — |
| mixed-scale.triple-product-vs-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | ENVELOPE: the subject REFUSES whenever the exact triple product needs more than 128 bits, even where the scaled result would have fitted the raw — three 64-bit factors reach 2^189 and the accumulator is 128 bits wide. That is a declined answer, never a wrong one, and the law models it exactly rather than tolerating it: the expected verdict is (width fits AND value fits), so a subject that widened its refusal or narrowed it would both fail | — | — | — |
| mobius.integer-0,-1 | law: Default | classical | — | QuadraticAlgebra<FixedQ4816>.MobiusStep numerator at the rotation relation (0, −1) — MobiusStepFusedInteger, plain wrapping long arithmetic, ZERO roundings | Oracles.MobiusNumerator in BigInteger, where the shift-16 RoundDyadic is provably a no-op (remainder identically zero at integer coefficients) — both sides exact, condition (B) drops out | — | — |
| mobius.integer-0,-1 | law: Default | structural | — | the projective step carries the input numerator forward unchanged as the returned denominator | — | — | — |
| mobius.integer-1,1 | law: Default | classical | — | QuadraticAlgebra<FixedQ4816>.MobiusStep numerator at the golden relation (1, 1) — MobiusStepFusedInteger, plain wrapping long arithmetic, ZERO roundings | Oracles.MobiusNumerator in BigInteger, where the shift-16 RoundDyadic is provably a no-op — both sides exact, condition (B) drops out | — | — |
| mobius.integer-1,1 | law: Default | structural | — | the projective step carries the input numerator forward unchanged as the returned denominator | — | — | — |
| mobius.integer-2,1 | law: Default | classical | — | QuadraticAlgebra<FixedQ4816>.MobiusStep numerator at the silver relation (2, 1) — MobiusStepFusedInteger, plain wrapping long arithmetic, ZERO roundings | Oracles.MobiusNumerator in BigInteger, where the shift-16 RoundDyadic is provably a no-op — both sides exact, condition (B) drops out | — | — |
| mobius.integer-2,1 | law: Default | structural | — | the projective step carries the input numerator forward unchanged as the returned denominator | — | — | — |
| ntt.convolution-aliasing-contract | law: Default | structural | — | Convolve(x, x, destination) with exact same-span operands is bit-identical to Convolve(copy(x), copy(x), destination) at lengths 1 through 1024. Partial operand overlap is refused naming right, and any destination overlap is refused naming destination; both refusals occur before either operand changes. This pins the dedicated one-forward self-convolution path and the zero-allocation overlap boundary. | — | — | — |
| ntt.convolution-vs-oracle | law: Default | classical | — | NumberTheoreticTransform.Convolve at lengths 1 through 1024 over Pcg32XshRr-seeded content, with the boundary values zero and Modulus - 1 forced onto the first one or two lanes | Oracles.CyclicConvolutionModulus — the O(N^2) definition-form sum in BigInteger, reduced once per output rather than diagonalized through a transform at all. The subject runs forward-forward-pointwise-inverse; the oracle never forwards, never inverts and never multiplies pointwise — the two share no algorithm, only the theorem that connects them. | — | — |
| ntt.convolution-vs-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | the comparison is EXACT equality, not a bound: field arithmetic never rounds, so a correct convolution theorem implementation reproduces the O(N^2) sum bit-for-bit. | — | — | — |
| ntt.length-refusals | law: Default | structural | — | every documented refusal, asserted by exception TYPE and by the parameter name it reports: NumberTheoreticTransformPlan.Create at zero, a negative length and a non-power-of-two length (3 and 6) — the largest power of two an int can name is 2^30, far below MaximumLog2Length, so no int length is ever refused for exceeding the prime's own two-adicity ceiling; Forward and Inverse given a span whose length does not equal the plan's; Convolve given a right or destination span of the wrong length; Convolve given a left span of the wrong length; PointwiseMultiply given a right span or a destination span whose length differs from left, each naming its own parameter. | — | — | — |
| ntt.linearity-exact | law: Default | structural | — | Forward(a) + Forward(b) == Forward(a + b) pointwise EXACTLY, at lengths 1 through 1024, where the addition on both sides is PrimeField64's own field Add — the DFT over a field is linear by the definition of the sum, and nothing here rounds, so the identity holds bit-for-bit rather than within a bound (the fixed-point FFT's linearity sibling, fft.linearity-bound, is the one that needs a bound). | — | — | — |
| ntt.pointwise-multiply-is-elementwise-product | law: Default | structural | — | PointwiseMultiply(left, right) is EXACTLY Field.Multiply(left[i], right[i]) at every lane for lengths 1 through 1024, including when destination is the exact same span as either operand. A shifted overlap is refused before writing, by exception type and destination parameter name. This is the public member's own value and alias contract; ntt.convolution-vs-oracle does not credit it because Convolve carries a private Montgomery-form multiplication loop and never calls PointwiseMultiply. | — | — | — |
| ntt.prime-and-primitive-root | law: Default | classical | — | NumberTheoreticTransform.Modulus and the declared odd factor 262111 of Modulus - 1, tested for primality | Oracles.ExactPrimality — trial division by the primes below 8192 then twenty independent strong-probable-prime rounds, sharing no code and no idea with PrimeField64.IsPrime's twelve-round witness set | — | — |
| ntt.prime-and-primitive-root | law: Default | structural | — | PrimeField64.IsPrime agrees with the independent oracle on both Modulus and the declared factor 262111, and 262111 * 2^44 + 1 equals Modulus exactly (the claimed factorization is re-derived from the two numbers rather than merely asserted) | — | — | — |
| ntt.prime-and-primitive-root | law: Default | classical | — | PrimitiveRoot's multiplicative order over Modulus, decided by BigInteger.ModPow at the group order and at the order divided by each of the two prime factors (2 and 262111) — the Pocklington-style certificate: a candidate generates the whole group of order c*2^k exactly when it is not one at either (c*2^k)/2 or (c*2^k)/262111 | BigInteger.ModPow, the BCL's own modular exponentiation, sharing no code with PrimeField64.Pow's Montgomery-ring chain (ScaledResidueRing64) | — | — |
| ntt.round-trip-exact | law: Default | structural | — | Inverse(Forward(x)) == x EXACTLY, bit-for-bit, at lengths 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64, 256 and 1024 over Pcg32XshRr-seeded field elements. Every step is exact field arithmetic (no rounding, no saturation anywhere in PrimeField64), so agreement is a bit-exact identity rather than a measured bound — a fused-substrate leg does not apply because nothing here rounds. | — | — | — |
| ntt.round-trip-exact | law: Default | structural | — | a wrong NumberTheoreticTransformPlan.Length getter breaks this case rather than passing it silently: NumberTheoreticTransform.Forward and Inverse both check the operand span's length against the plan's Length before running, so a Length that answered anything other than the length the plan was built for throws on every call this case makes, which Laws.Claim reports as a failure. | — | — | — |
| polynomial.additive-group-and-accessors | law: Default | classical | — | BinaryPolynomial.Degree — sixty-three minus a hardware LeadingZeroCount over the packed carrier (BinaryPolynomial.cs:53) | Oracles.BinaryPolynomialDegree, a downward scan in BigInteger for the highest set bit that knows nothing of a carrier width, so a wrong width constant or an off-by-one in the complement is visible. EXACT on both sides: this wing rounds nowhere, so the substrate condition is not merely discharged, it does not arise | — | — |
| polynomial.additive-group-and-accessors | law: Default | classical | — | BinaryPolynomial.operator + and operator −, both of which are one ulong exclusive or (BinaryPolynomial.cs:63-70) | Oracles.BinaryPolynomialSum — the coefficient sum formed ARITHMETICALLY, one bit position at a time, as an integer addition reduced modulo two rather than a bitwise operator, so a subject that reached for a conjunction, a disjunction or an ordinary sum is caught | — | — |
| polynomial.additive-group-and-accessors | law: Default | classical | — | BinaryPolynomial.ToString over the swept operands, a six-row written-form ladder hand-derived from the convention, and the dense sixty-four-term word stated by its shape — term count, opening exponent and closing pair | Oracles.BinaryPolynomialText, which collects terms into a list and joins them and takes its upper bound from the CALLER rather than from Degree, where the subject walks Degree downward into a StringBuilder placing a separator before each term after the first. ENVELOPE: the member's own doc says the form is diagnostic and claims NO parsing round trip, so this leg pins the rendering and nothing about a reader. It buys NO coverage credit — MemberSurface.ExcludedNames drops ToString (Coverage.cs:19-23) — and stands because a reversed exponent loop or a misplaced separator is otherwise invisible | — | — |
| polynomial.additive-group-and-accessors | law: Default | structural | — | the constructor and Bits round trip over the whole sixty-four-bit carrier: every swept raw, reinterpreted unchanged, reads back bit-for-bit | — | — | — |
| polynomial.additive-group-and-accessors | law: Default | structural | — | characteristic two, stated three ways at every swept operand: unary minus is the identity map, a polynomial added to itself is zero, and subtraction IS addition — the type's whole additive contract | — | — | — |
| polynomial.additive-group-and-accessors | law: Default | structural | — | the five declared constants read into locals before comparison so the run makes the comparison rather than the compiler: Zero equals AdditiveIdentity equals default with Bits zero, IsZero true, IsOne false and Degree −1; One equals MultiplicativeIdentity with Bits one, IsOne true and Degree zero; Indeterminate has Bits two and Degree one. A swap of any two of them reddens here | — | — | — |
| polynomial.additive-group-and-accessors | law: Default | structural | — | Zero is the two-sided identity for both + and − at every swept operand, and commutativity and associativity of + hold over three distinct operands | — | — | — |
| polynomial.divrem-vs-monomial-oracle | law: Default | classical | — | BinaryPolynomial.DivRem — top-down long division, aligning the divisor's leading term against the running remainder's and clearing one high coefficient per step (BinaryPolynomial.cs:195-212) | Oracles.BinaryPolynomialDivRem — the BOTTOM-UP monomial route, which carries the pair (t^i div d, t^i mod d) forward one exponent at a time and sums the pairs at the dividend's set bits, never inspecting the dividend's leading term at all. Two different derivations of the same unique pair; EXACT on both sides, so the substrate condition does not arise. ENVELOPE on the operand stream: a zero divisor divides nothing, so a drawn zero divisor is replaced by One — applied IDENTICALLY in the subject and in the oracle — and the zero divisor's own contract is the refusal leg below | — | — |
| polynomial.divrem-vs-monomial-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | the division identity, at every swept pair: (quotient · divisor) + remainder is the dividend BIT-FOR-BIT. ENVELOPE, stated rather than implied: the product here is exact only because deg(quotient) + deg(divisor) equals deg(dividend), which is at most 63 — the identity leans on the truncating operator NOT truncating on these operands, and polynomial.multiply-vs-carryless-oracle is where the truncation itself is pinned | — | — | — |
| polynomial.divrem-vs-monomial-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | the remainder's degree is strictly below the divisor's at every swept pair, which is the half of Euclidean division the identity alone does not force | — | — | — |
| polynomial.divrem-vs-monomial-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | the refusal contract: DivRem, operator / and operator % each throw DivideByZeroException against the zero polynomial, checked at every swept dividend INCLUDING the zero one, where a guard that tested the dividend instead would pass unnoticed | — | — | — |
| polynomial.divrem-vs-monomial-oracle | law: Default | structural | — | the four poles: the zero dividend gives (Zero, Zero); a divisor of strictly higher degree gives (Zero, dividend) with no loop iteration at all; a non-zero polynomial divided by itself gives (One, Zero); and division by One gives (dividend, Zero) — the degenerate cases the sampled stream reaches only by accident | — | — | — |
| polynomial.divrem-vs-monomial-oracle | law: Default | shared-substrate | delegation-twin | BinaryPolynomial.operator / and operator % | DivRem's Quotient and Remainder | DivRem itself — both operators are one call through to it (BinaryPolynomial.cs:100-108), so agreement proves the projection and never the division | the classical leg above, in this same case, on the same operand stream: the pair the two operators project out of is pinned against Oracles.BinaryPolynomialDivRem before either operator reads it |
| polynomial.factor-odd-cycle-vs-cyclotomic-cosets | law: Default | classical | — | the DEGREES of BinaryPolynomial.FactorOddCycle's output at each ladder order (BinaryPolynomial.cs:151-189) | Oracles.BinaryCyclotomicFactorDegrees — the orbit sizes of x ↦ 2x on Z/nZ. The classical structure of t^n − 1 over GF(2): the Frobenius map permutes the n-th roots of unity by squaring and each orbit is the root set of one irreducible factor. NO polynomial is multiplied, divided or reduced anywhere in that computation, where the subject enumerates monic candidates, tests each for irreducibility and divides — the two sides could not fail together. | presented.clifford-quaternion-even-twin | law: Default | shared-substrate | fused-substrate | the even (3,0,0) embedding of two quaternions (i ↔ -e23, j ↔ e13, k ↔ -e12) under GeometricAlgebra.GeometricProduct, full raw range less the ENVELOPE fold below, then read back and required to stay in the even subalgebra (GeometricAlgebra.IsEven) | FixedQuaternion.op_Multiply (the Hamilton product) | FixedQ4816.RoundProductSum(long) and (Int128) — the IDENTICAL kernel on both sides (GeometricAlgebra.cs:190,221; FixedQuaternion.cs:111-114,116-119) | ENVELOPE: the embedding negates the swept quaternion's X and Z components (i ↔ -e23, k ↔ -e12). FixedQ4816.MinValue's unary negation is documented to wrap rather than throw (FixedQ4816.cs's operator- remarks) because MinValue's positive magnitude is exactly 2^47, one raw past MaxValue and therefore unrepresentable in FixedQ4816 at all — not a defect of negation, and not something any FixedQ4816 blade coefficient could hold either. A swept X or Z of exactly long.MinValue therefore embeds as itself instead of the +2^47 this sign convention requires, corrupting entry to GeometricProduct: this was the twin's counterexample (left=[0,1,0,0] right=[0,0,-9223372036854775808,0], lane=0, +2^47 vs -2^47). GeometricAlgebraClaims.ExcludeUnembeddableMinValue folds exactly that one raw value on X and Z (both operands) onto MinValue+1, whose negation is exact; Y and W (never negated by this embedding) keep the full raw range including MinValue unchanged |

| presented.letter-mask-refuses-a-split-block | law: Default | structural | — | a letter is the smallest thing a mask can name, so LettersOf refuses a predicate that SPLITS one rather than broadening it. On tokens {1,2,3} refined against Full there is a single letter, and both the token-1 and the token-{1,2} predicates cut it: each raises an ArgumentException naming 'predicate' whose message names letter 0 and says it is split. Intersection alone previously returned that whole letter, so a pattern built from the mask accepted tokens 2 and 3 that the predicate rejects — a broadened language, silently, with no refusal anywhere downstream | — | — | — |

The derivation routes differ where the kernels branch: the subject folds Add with ONE conditional subtraction that leans on p < 2^62, writes Subtract as a borrow-avoiding two-arm compare, and widens Multiply to UInt128 for a single hardware remainder, where the oracle forms each value in arbitrary width and takes one remainder with no case analysis at all | — | — |

| prime-field.baillie-composition | law: Default | classical | — | PrimeField64.IsBaillieProbablePrime over the swept candidate stream, forced odd | Oracles.ExactPrimality — the exact decision, outside Puck.Maths entirely. ENVELOPE, the same one the two IsPrime laws state and stated again because this stream lives almost entirely above it: through 8191² = 67092481 that oracle decides by TRIAL DIVISION alone and shares no idea with the subject, but above that band it runs twenty BigInteger strong-probable-prime rounds whose base set OPENS WITH TWO — the very round that is one of the two halves of IsBaillieProbablePrime. So above the trial-division band subject and oracle share that CRITERION, differing in arithmetic (one shared ScaledResidueRing64 against plain residues), in base set and in loop structure; the swept stream draws full-width raws, so essentially every candidate lands there. What this leg pins independently is the Lucas half and the composition, not the base-two round in isolation — prime-field.strong-round-vs-oracle owns that. Below 2^64 the composition is not merely unrefuted but VERIFIED counterexample-free: Feitsma and Galway independently enumerated the complete set of base-two Fermat pseudoprimes below 2^64 (the strong ones being a derived subset) and no member is simultaneously a strong Lucas pseudoprime for Selfridge Method A, which is exactly what this implementation runs. ulong IS that region, so nothing here is extrapolated and the equality is asserted flatly. The failure message says outright that a disagreement below 2^64 is either a defect or the first known counterexample — which is the honest reading, not a hedge | — | — |
| prime-field.baillie-composition | law: Default | structural | — | the CARRIAGE, read back rather than assumed: IsBaillieProbablePrime is exactly IsStrongProbablePrime(value, 2) AND IsStrongLucasProbablePrime(value), both halves evaluated separately and the conjunction compared. That is one line of source, and a line that could carry a disjunction or transposed operands — neither of which the differential against a primality oracle would show. It is asserted on a FIXED ladder as well as on the swept stream, and the ladder is where it actually bites: on any sampled stream the two halves AGREE at every candidate — every prime passes both, every composite fails both, which is exactly the Baillie-PSW guarantee — so the conjunction is decidable only at the published pseudoprime populations, where the round accepts alone at 2047 and the Lucas half accepts alone at 5459. The claim body COUNTS both directions and fails if the ladder ever stops carrying one | — | — | — |
| prime-field.baillie-composition | law: Default | structural | — | ENVELOPE, measured rather than assumed, and it corrects what a reader would expect: the WITNESS BASE in that line is NOT pinned by this law or by anything else in the suite. Swapping the base two for the base three moves no answer at any odd value below 10^7, and a value below 2^64 that moved one would have to be a composite passing both the base-three round and the strong Lucas test — a Baillie-PSW counterexample in its own right, of exactly the class Feitsma and Galway's enumeration rules out for base two. A DEGENERATE base is a different matter and IS caught: bases 0, 1 and value itself all collapse the round to a constant true, and the ladder's Lucas-pseudoprime rows reject that at 5459 | — | — | — |
| prime-field.baillie-composition | law: Default | in-tree-independent | — | IsBaillieProbablePrime over the same stream | PrimeField64.IsPrime, the twelve-base decision — a second shipped route to the same answers, and a comparison that would become a TAUTOLOGY if IsPrime were ever re-pointed at this composition — reading green while testing nothing, because both sides would then be the same decision | — | both sides are PrimeField64, so this leg is not independent evidence about the field's arithmetic; what makes it worth declaring is that the two decisions rest on different theorems. IsPrime is itself anchored classically in prime-field.is-prime-vs-sieve-and-witness-ladder against a sieve of Eratosthenes over 0..20,000 and against Oracles.ExactPrimality on the carrier ladder. If IsPrime is re-pointed, THIS leg goes vacuous and must be deleted — the classical leg above does not, because its reference is outside Puck.Maths |
| prime-field.baillie-composition | law: Default | structural | — | ENVELOPE: this law SAMPLES where prime-field.baillie-psw-exhaustive is exhaustive at EVERY one of the 4,294,967,296 values a uint holds — against a segmented sieve of Eratosthenes, not against another Puck.Maths decision — and where it replays 160,000 sampled and 60,000 contiguous values to ulong.MaxValue against Oracles.ExactPrimality. That law is the gate of record for SCALE, at the Exhaustive tier; the statements are here, at Default. Neither replaces the other | — | — | — |
| prime-field.baillie-psw-exhaustive | law: Exhaustive | classical | — | PrimeField64.IsBaillieProbablePrime at EVERY one of the 4,294,967,296 values a uint holds, and PrimeField64.IsStrongLucasProbablePrime required to accept every prime among them | a SEGMENTED sieve of Eratosthenes written in PrimalityScaleClaims.cs, run block by block over the whole 32-bit range. Both halves of the composition are PROBABLE-prime tests with infinitely many pseudoprimes each, so the composition earns its trust from evidence; this leg is that evidence, and it makes the statement below 2^32 a COMPUTED fact rather than a cited one — no known counterexample becomes none exists. The reference shares with the subject not merely no code but no idea, and is not a second Puck.Maths kernel. The work is embarrassingly parallel and the VERDICT is not — each block records only its own least disagreement and the blocks are read in ascending order — so a rerun reports the same value. Measured: about five minutes on six cores | — | — |
| prime-field.baillie-psw-exhaustive | law: Exhaustive | classical | — | PrimeField64.IsStrongLucasProbablePrime at every value below 200,000 and at 20,000 full-width odd values | Oracles.StrongLucasSelfridge — the same test computed from 2×2 COMPANION-MATRIX powers in BigInteger. Three deliberate divergences: the subject walks the U/V doubling identities most-significant-bit first with halvings on every index-incrementing step, entirely inside a Montgomery ring, while the oracle multiplies matrices in plain residues, halves nothing, and carries no V recurrence at all. Its Selfridge search also takes its symbol from Oracles.JacobiSymbolReciprocity rather than from any shipped Jacobi, which is what closes the OWED standing over a Lucas oracle's own symbol source | — | — |
| prime-field.baillie-psw-exhaustive | law: Exhaustive | classical | — | PrimeField64.IsStrongProbablePrime over eight witness bases — including the degenerate zero and one and both carrier edges — at every value below 20,000, plus 2,000 full-width value/witness pairs, and the documented degenerate vectors including 341, the base-two FERMAT pseudoprime that is not a STRONG one | Oracles.ModularStrongProbablePrime — one strong round in plain BigInteger residues, where the subject makes its whole acceptance test against a Montgomery ring's encoded constants and never leaves that form. The first half needs an oracle of its own, or a witness-round fault and a Lucas fault could CANCEL inside the conjunction and neither differential would see it | — | — |

Below 2^64 the composition is not merely unrefuted but VERIFIED counterexample-free: Feitsma and Galway independently enumerated the complete set of base-two Fermat pseudoprimes below 2^64 and no member is simultaneously a strong Lucas pseudoprime for Selfridge Method A, which is exactly what this implementation runs, so nothing here is extrapolated. The failure message says outright that a disagreement below 2^64 is either a defect or the first known counterexample. The reference is outside the library entirely rather than a second decision in the same class, such as PrimeField64.IsPrime | — | — |
